figures.caption: Fig. 2. The VLMM map projected on real AI2-THOR keyframes (exact-GT sim); rows are three scenes. The first two columns are the input RGB and depth; the next three are natural-language queries, each routed to a single schema field: “what is moving” (→observed motion), “things I could move” (→movability prior), “where it stays still” (→motion class=STATIC). Highlighted instances are the query result (tiny movers are ring-marked; dimmed = not selected). The attributes are object-level instances, not a per-voxel feature volume.

Fig. 4. Query “what is moving” made visible (one THOR scene, exact-GT sim; top-N shown, N=#GT movers). The semantic-only baseline ranks by CLIP similarity to “an object that is currently moving” (Table II row i, F1≈0.10) and returns the wrong instances; VLMM ranks by observed motion and returns exactly the ground-truth movers (green rings). Built from the same pinned map as Table II.

Fig. 1. VLMM builds each element from two channels and routes each query to one field. The range-dependent depth-covariance box (teal) is what neither prior system represents in an open-vocabulary, language-queryable map; it makes the motion attribute uncertainty-aware.

Fig. 5. Calibration and pose robustness. (a) raw motion confidence is uncalibrated (ECE 0.30); (b) post-hoc isotonic calibration, fit on TUM and tested held-out on Bonn, reaches ECE 0.10. (c,d) ego-refinement makes moving-vs-static AP invariant to estimated-pose error; without it AP degrades.
